title: epic: every cam command is deterministic CLI or a spawned pane with structured handback; orch only converses, decides, narrates
description: Finish the migration the project already proved in slices (CAM-149 removed the LLM from ship, CAM-190 from backlog queries, plan-runner from plan control flow): no /cam-* skill executes work inside the orchestrator context. Three target layers, from the 2026-07-06 inventory of .claude/commands/. Layer 1, mechanizable to pure deterministic CLI (zero LLM, no pane): cam-prune (43 lines of inline git steps), cam status (does not exist yet: one command rendering the cycle state-machine position: phase, in-flight PRD, pending stories, container preflight, merge-watch, wedge and stall markers, plus a why-not-moving diagnosis; consumes CAM-195 events and markers), cam-next pre-flight checks (118 lines currently run in the orch session), cam issue get. Layer 2, LLM-needing but non-interactive, always a spawned pane with structured handback (worker-report.json plus one-line send-keys push, the CAM-75/77/78 comms decision): cam-issue create free-text expansion (today asymmetric: terminal thin-proxy already spawns a pane, orch-invoked path runs inline), cam-review orchestration (216 lines run in orch context while the reviewer subagent already runs in a pane; target: thin signal-writer like plan and ship since the sidecar drives review rounds). Layer 3, LLM plus operator-interactive: cam-spec grill moves to its own pane with handback (interview transcript has zero value to the long-lived orch context after the spec lands on main; a 50k-token grill inside the orch contradicts the one-PR-per-session invariant). Layer 3 is ADR-worthy (hard to reverse, real trade-off: single human-facing interface vs orch context preservation) and must be resolved in the grill of this epic. Every spawned pane documents its contract and reports completion to the orch via the structured handback channel, never via pane scrollback parsing. Slice at spec time into near-independent PRs (project lesson: 2 changes = 2 PRs). Dedupe against CAM-153 (plan-runner gates cluster), CAM-52 (structured outputs), CAM-63 (supervisor-worker boundary), CAM-196 (meta_loop-aware boot narration). Origin: operator direction 2026-07-06 after the CAM-118 wedge audit showed the orch re-deriving operational state every session instead of running one deterministic command.
